messages:
Sarah S.: incoming support ticket from ACME — sharp spike in 5xx after the 15:00 deploy. customer says multiple requests returning 502/504 and timeouts. ticket: SUP-12345. stack: hosted inference (api.redwood).
Alex K.: @Sarah can you paste a quick example request id or curl so we can repro? :eyes:
Sarah S.: here's a sample request id they captured: req=acme-req-20260315-88a7. They sent a minimal prompt + metadata, usually fine. Also attached a short trace: 
```
ERROR 15:05:12 gateway: upstream 502 EdgeHandler: kvcache-miss -> auth-fail? token rejected, attempt=1
ERROR 15:05:13 router: request timeout after 12s
```
Maya P.: seeing telemetry — small canary at 10% rolled at 15:00, then ramp to 40% at 15:02 (auto). 5xx rate on canary pods jumped from 0.2% -> 9% within 2m. :rotating_light:
Priya R.: interesting — auth plugin changed in this roll (flag: prefetch-auth-enabled=true). Could be auth header trimming at the proxy. That would explain remote 401->502 mapping. Need header capture.
Sarah S.: customer also reported billing anomalies — some calls charged as errors and counted as units. BillingOps, can you flag SUP-12345? they care about credits.
BillingOps: flagged, will hold charges pending incident. send invoice hold to customer.
Alex K.: repro attempt: using their request id with the same model/version fails behind our gateway. Quick curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_KEY>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
returns 502 with body: `{ "error": "upstream error: connection reset" }` on canary nodes. Non-canary returns 200.
Maya P.: DeployBot shows config keys for the rollout: kernel=v2, prefetch=true, auth-header-trim=on, batch-window=20ms. I suspect auth-header-trim is too aggressive for some clients.
Priya R.: repro steps for infra team: 1) route 100% traffic to canary in staging -> observe kvcache misses. 2) enable header logging on proxy for that slice. 3) check auth validator logs for header normalization. I'll take step 2.
Alex K.: granted, rolling an immediate pause of the staged ramp. Can someone stop the auto-ramp? @DeployBot please.
DeployBot: [automation] pausing rollout for release r-20260315-15:00. current weight: 40%.
Actions: pause, snapshot telemetry.
Maya P.: snapshot shows request header length truncated to 128 bytes on canary proxy (old threshold was 512). That aligns with auth header trim flag.
Sarah S.: customer confirmed they saw truncated bearer tokens -> got mapped to 401 upstream which our gateway surfaced as 502. They provided an example token prefix that was shortened.
Priya R.: plan: rollback the flag change in canary -> restore header length to 512 -> validate with sample token. Who can do the rollback? Alex?
Alex K.: I'll push rollback to canary now. patch: set auth-header-trim=false on rollout config and redeploy canary slice. executing at 15:16 UTC.
DeployBot: [automation] applying config change to canary r-20260315-15:00 -> set auth-header-trim=false. new canary weight remains 40% until manual.
Maya P.: after config flip, 5xx on canary dropped to 0.3% within 90s. sample request that previously failed now returns 200 and token validated. :thumbsup:
Sarah S.: pinged customer with update and asked them to confirm. They reported successful passes for 10/10 calls in their next batch.
BillingOps: marking charges for SUP-12345 as under review; initiating credit for failed requests. Will follow up with accounting.
Alex K.: follow-ups: create rollback hotpatch doc, add test that verifies header length >= 512 in canary smoke tests, and gate prefetch-auth-enabled behind an integration test.
Priya R.: I'll own the postmortem and link to the config diff: /deploys/r-20260315-15:00/diff. Also recommend a short-term rule: block trimming of Authorization header for hosted inference endpoints.
Sarah S.: closing loop with customer now. Thanks everyone for quick turnaround.

---
Summary: cause = new auth-header-trim flag in canary truncating bearer tokens -> upstream auth fails -> gateway returned 502/504. Mitigation = paused rollout + reverted flag in canary -> 5xx rates returned to baseline. Next steps = postmortem + billing credits for customer.
